evidence_detail: All 4 DOIs resolve to real journal articles (Crossref + ThermoML citation blocks): 10.1016/j.fluid.2013.12.014 = Guo-Zhu Jia & Qian, 'Dielectric constant of dimethyl sulfoxide-monohydric alcohol mixture solution at the microwave frequency', Fluid Phase Equilib. 365:5-10 (2014); 10.1021/je3007666 = Klimaszewski/Borun/Bald/Sengwa, 'Static Permittivities of Isomeric Butanol Mixtures at Temperatures from (288.15 to 308.15) K', J. Chem. Eng. Data 57:3164-3170 (2012); 10.1021/je800593p = Chmielewska/Zurada/Klimaszewski/Bald, 'Dielectric Properties of Methanol Mixtures with Ethanol, Isomers of Propanol, and Butanol', J. Chem. Eng. Data 54:801-806 (2009); 10.1021/je900503p = Farhan & Awwad, 'Relative Permittivities, Refractive Indices, and Densities of Dihydrofuran-2(3H)-one + Butan-1-ol and + Butan-2-ol at T = (293.15, 298.15, 303.15, and 313.15) K', J. Chem. Eng. Data 55:1035-1038 (2010). NOT 4 INDEPENDENT EXPERIMENTS. Primary ThermoML XML extraction shows the 298.15 K pair je3007666/je800593p is byte-identical (eps=16.60, u95=0.06, 'Dielectrometer', same Klimaszewski/Bald group) - a duplicate transcription, not a replication, matching duplicate_observation_groups.csv. je900503p's neat-butanol entries are also non-independent: identical to the Klimaszewski cluster at 293.15 K (17.51) and 303.15 K (15.75) INCLUDING the identical expanded uncertainty 0.06, and 16.58 at 298.15 K sits 0.02 from 16.60 - i.e. literature-tabulated pure-component values in a mixture paper, not an independent measurement by Farhan & Awwad. After deduplication only 2 genuinely independent experiments remain: the Klimaszewski/Bald dielectrometer series (16.60 +/- 0.06, u95; 0.36% relative) and Guo-Zhu & Qian's microwave-network-analyser point (17.60 +/- 1.90, u95; 10.8% relative, T recorded as 298 with 3 digits). The residual difference is 1.00 in eps against a combined standard uncertainty of 0.95 = 1.05 sigma, and only 0.53x the combined 95% expanded uncertainty: the two independent experiments AGREE within their stated uncertainties. The 6.15% 'spread' is an artefact of (a) counting one duplicated experiment three times and (b) including a low-precision point whose own 95% interval [15.70, 19.50] contains 16.60. The 298 K vs 298.15 K binning contributes only ~0.03 in eps (d eps/dT = -0.177/K), so binning is not the cause. Conclusion: no genuine conflict; KEEP the v06 value 16.60, which is the highest-precision primary measurement (J. Chem. Eng. Data, dedicated isomeric-butanol study) and is consistent with the only other independent experiment. Recommend collapsing the 4 source DOIs to 2 evidence units in any downstream 'n independent sources' claim.

All 3 DOIs resolve to real journal articles (Crossref + ThermoML citation blocks): 10.1016/j.fluid.2008.01.024 = Sengwa/Khatri/Sankhla, 'Dielectric properties and hydrogen bonding interaction behaviour in binary mixtures of glycerol with amides and amines', Fluid Phase Equilib. 266:54-58 (2008); 10.1016/j.fluid.2009.07.009 = Sengwa/Sankhla/Khatri, 'Dielectric constant and molecular association in binary mixtures of N,N-dimethylethanolamine with alcohols and amides', Fluid Phase Equilib. 285:50-53 (2009); 10.1021/je9002515 = Swiergiel & Jadzyn, 'Static Dielectric Permittivity and Electric Conductivity of N-Methylacetamide + N,N-Dimethylacetamide Mixtures', J. Chem. Eng. Data 54:2296-2300 (2009). NOT 3 INDEPENDENT EXPERIMENTS. The two Fluid Phase Equilibria papers are the SAME three authors (Sengwa, Khatri, Sankhla) in permuted order and give a byte-identical neat-DMAc point at 303.15 K: eps=37.72 with identical expanded uncertainty u95=0.23, matching duplicate_observation_groups.csv and the source_independence_report (5 shared observations across this document pair). This is a duplicate transcription, not a replication. After deduplication only 2 genuinely independent experiments remain, and THEY GENUINELY DISAGREE: Sengwa 37.72 +/- 0.23 (u95) vs Swiergiel & Jadzyn 38.67 +/- 0.387 (u95). Difference 0.95 against a combined standard uncertainty of 0.225 = 4.22 sigma (2.11x the combined 95% expanded uncertainty). Unlike conflict 1, this conflict is NOT an artefact of duplication and does NOT disappear on deduplication - it is created by the deduplication, because the duplicated pair had been masking a single-group outlier position against a well-documented temperature series. Quality ranking: 10.1021/je9002515 is the strongest record - a dedicated primary dielectric study with DMAc as a principal objective, a self-consistent 10-point series from 303.15 to 393.15 K (38.67 down to 24.923), and a documented 99.5% purity stated by supplier; its local slope (-0.212/K) back-extrapolates to eps(298.15 K) = 37.61, close to the widely cited anchor 37.78. The Sengwa values are by-products of mixture studies (DMAc is a minor component in glycerol+amide and N,N-dimethylethanolamine+amide systems), reported at a single temperature with no series and hence no internal consistency check, and the 2009 record carries a compiler-ESTIMATED purity of only 98% for a strongly hygroscopic solvent whose water content is not recorded in ThermoML. Both values also sit near distinct literature clusters (37.78 and ~38.9), so neither can be dismissed on priors, and both groups used a parallel-plate capacitor method on a conductive liquid (Swiergiel measured conductivity alongside permittivity), making low-frequency electrode-polarisation correction the most likely discriminator. That detail - frequency range, low-frequency extrapolation/correction, and sample water content - is in the primary PDFs and is absent from the metadata. Therefore HOLD: the conflict is real, bounded (2.52%), and cannot be honestly closed from bibliographic metadata alone. Do not silently keep 37.72. Action: obtain the three primary PDFs, check the water-content/purity statement and the frequency/extrapolation protocol, then either adopt the better-supported value or, if both survive, retain a single value with the 0.95 (2.5%) disagreement recorded as a documented label uncertainty rather than deleting either experiment.
